name: Agent Memory and Planning
blurb: How agents remember, plan, and recover.

repos.name: mem0
repos.description: Universal memory layer for AI Agents

repos.name: letta
repos.description: Platform for stateful agents: AI with advanced memory that can learn and self-improve over time.

reading.body:
Agent memory tooling has consolidated quickly around a small number of actively maintained open-source projects, with three repositories together holding nearly 94,000 GitHub stars under identical Apache-2.0 licences.

mem0 leads by a wide margin at over 64,000 stars, positioning itself as a general-purpose memory layer that any agent can attach to. Letta follows at roughly 24,500 stars, with an explicit focus on stateful agents that learn and self-improve over time. Zep, at just under 5,000 stars, is the smallest of the three and the only one whose description does not specify a clear architectural role from the data given. All three repositories received commits within the final days of August 2026, which confirms active development rather than maintenance mode.

Memory and planning matter for AI infrastructure because stateless inference is cheap but limited. Once an agent must retain context across sessions, retrieve prior decisions, or adjust its behaviour from accumulated experience, the compute requirement changes shape: reads and writes to persistent memory add latency, storage, and retrieval costs that sit between the model and the user. The data here covers only the open-source software layer. It says nothing about the hardware, the power draw, or the data-centre footprint that running these systems at scale would require, and it covers only three projects, so it does not establish what the full landscape of agent memory tooling looks like.
